# cm021: divergences the patch does not record

## A brand or bulk mailbox with no list header is machine mail (CM051 F7, walk #16)

Tree `cm021`. NEW CM051-side behaviour. `src/cli.py` gains `automated_address_reason` and its constants (inserted immediately above the "An organisation writing from a personal-looking address" comment) and `automated_sender_reason` calls it last, after the list/bulk/auto-submitted headers, the local-part regex and the display-name rule. "Quidco" (local part `quidco`, sub-domain `info.`) and "HSBC Hong Kong" (local part `onlineservices`, sub-domain `notification.`) became People because their mail carried no list header this parser sees, and neither the local part nor the display name read as automated. The address does: a bulk-mail sub-domain (`info.`, `notification.`, `emails.`), a local part equal to the sender's own domain name, or an automation stem (`service`, `statement`, `noreply` ...). Existing reason labels are unchanged (the display-name rule still runs first).

### What a future sync must preserve

`automated_address_reason` and its call at the end of `automated_sender_reason`. Guarded by `tests/test_people_have_human_evidence.py` (`test_cm021_refuses_a_brand_mailbox_with_no_list_header`, `test_the_two_copies_of_the_address_rule_agree`) and the unchanged `tests/test_automated_senders_are_not_people.py`. Retire by landing the same change in CM021 and re-pinning.

## The email ingest upserts onto the live survivor of a merged person (DMG #27, shape sweep S2)

Tree `cm021`. NEW CM051-side behaviour. `src/cli.py` gains `_live_person_iri` (inserted immediately above `_sparql_select`), which follows `pwg:mergedInto` to the live survivor; the per-message upsert in `cmd_mbox` passes `_live_person_iri(args.graph_endpoint, _safe_person_iri(addr))` to `_build_upsert`. `_build_upsert` writes `rdf:type pwg:Person` onto the IRI it is given, and the IRI is minted from the address, so after a merge every tick re-typed the merged-away node as a Person. A store error raises inside the existing per-message `try`, which records the error type and writes nothing (fail closed).

### What a future sync must preserve

`_live_person_iri` and its use at the `_build_upsert` call. Guarded by `tests/test_merged_people_are_not_recreated.py::test_email_ingest_upserts_onto_the_survivor`. Retire by landing the same change in CM021 and re-pinning.

## Notification-subject and gibberish display names do not become people (Andy's #30 console walk)

Tree `cm021`. NEW CM051-side behaviour, extending the existing F7 graft. `src/cli.py` gains `clean_display_name`, `_has_escaping_artefact` and `_is_gibberish_name` (inserted immediately above `looks_like_subject_or_sender_id`), and `looks_like_subject_or_sender_id` now (1) refuses a name carrying a quoting/escaping artefact (`~~`, a backslash-escaped quote, or a leading tilde/quote/backslash) and evaluates its other arms against the CLEANED name, and (2) refuses a name with a letter+digit mash token (an extraction artefact). The per-message upsert in `cmd_mbox` writes `clean_display_name(raw_name)` on the kept path. On the walk box a People node was named `~~\"Unusual sign-in on your iCloud.` -- an Apple security-notification SUBJECT whose leading `~~\"` sat before the first word and shielded the sentence-opener arm -- and others were gibberish ("03thom Hqn4828ra", "21ftcl Kzi6749lj"). Both shapes now classify as not-a-name. Pre-existing positives (sentence openers, `#`/alphanumeric sender ids, `<name> via <service>`) and real names (accents, hyphens, apostrophes, a 2-char surname, a `Jr.` suffix) are unchanged.

### What a future sync must preserve

`clean_display_name`, `_has_escaping_artefact`, `_is_gibberish_name`, the two new arms inside `looks_like_subject_or_sender_id`, and the `clean_display_name(raw_name)` write in `cmd_mbox`. Guarded by `tests/test_junk_names_are_not_people.py`. Retire by landing the same change in CM021 and re-pinning (blocked today: a full cm021 re-vendor still carries operator-PII, see the manifest note).
